beats.say: Japan just launched a historic mission to collect rocks from Mars's moon Phobos.
According to the Guardian, the unmanned probe was propelled by Japan's flagship H3 rocket.
The spacecraft is expected to reach Mars's orbit in August next year and collect at least 10g of soil and rock from the surface of Phobos.
The Guardian reports that the five-year mission is scheduled to return in 2031.

facts: Japan has successfully launched a spacecraft on an unprecedented mission to bring back samples from one of Mars’s moons.
The Martian Moons Exploration spacecraft was propelled by Japan’s flagship H3 rocket.
The spacecraft is expected to reach Mars’s orbit in August next year and collect at least 10g of soil and rock from the surface of Phobos.
The mission is scheduled to return in 2031.
